title: SkillOpt, described as a Microsoft open-source 'training manager' that reviews your Claude Code sessions for repeated corrections and proposes edits to your skill files overnight

tools.name: SkillOpt
tools.detail: 'Microsoft / open source'; no URL or repo path shown; UI text 'Review. Improve. Validate. Proposals ready for your review.'

claims: SkillOpt reviews your Claude Code sessions, spots recurring corrections (e.g. 'add the next steps' every report) and proposes improvements to the skill's instructions
Run it overnight, review suggested improvements in the morning
Pitched as 'Claude learns while you sleep' / 'you wanted an assistant, not another employee to train'
how_to_steps: Point SkillOpt at your Claude Code session history
It diffs your corrections against the skill instructions that produced the output
It proposes an instruction change (e.g. 'Always include next steps, owners and deadlines')
on_screen_only: 'MICROSOFT / OPEN SOURCE  SkillOpt.  A training manager for your AI.'
Diagram: Claude Code sessions (Report drafting, Your correction, The recurring pattern) -> Report-writing skill (Instructions Claude follows -> 'Improve the rule behind the output')
Example before/after: 'Write a clear weekly report.' -> 'Always include next steps, owners and deadlines.' / 'Choose an owner. Set a deadline.'
Timeline 'Overnight -> Morning review'; 'SUGGESTED IMPROVEMENT Report-writing skill'

relevance.why: Automating the loop Haji already does manually with his session-learning skill (mine sessions -> propose skill updates) would save real time, if the tool is real.

implement_score.why: If it exists and reads Claude Code transcripts locally, it is a drop-in complement to session-learning; otherwise the idea can be replicated with a nightly Routine that runs the existing session-learning skill over the day's transcripts.

verify: Does a Microsoft 'SkillOpt' repo exist? No URL shown; name/attribution may be wrong or hype
Does it work with Claude Code transcripts or only with its own agent framework?
Does it send session content to a cloud service?

gap.what: A tool for automated skill-instruction optimization from correction history; liked set had Karpathy skills and manual code-quality skills but nothing that rewrites skills from session feedback.
